text:
maria: quick sanity-check — i'm sketching an RFC follow-up for the continuous-batching scheduler. the core idea is a small-window unified path that tries to absorb microbursts without creating separate tiny-queue islands. want tradeoff notes before i write the doc.

alex: tl;dr: sounds promising. main worry is starvation when small-window requests hold kv-cache pointers for too long.

maria: exactly — my thought is to attach a soft lease + eviction hint so small-window requests can be preempted once they hit a headroom limit. preempt -> requeue with lower priority.

sam: are we conflating two orthogonal things: (1) admission shaping for latency vs throughput, and (2) kv-cache lifecycle. we should keep interfaces separate.

maria: agreed we should separate APIs. proposal: scheduler exposes admission hints + deadline; runtime exposes kv_eviction_hint(request_id, priority_hint). they can be implemented independently.

dina: +1. also we need a simple way to opt into unified small-window path per tenant. not everyone wants preemption semantics. config example: 

```
small_window: {
  enabled: true,
  max_hold_ms: 25,
  preempt_policy: "soft-requeue",
  headroom_tokens: 8
}
```

alex: nit: why 25ms? that seems aggressive for some gpus. maybe make it percentile-driven (p95 of warmup) rather than fixed.

maria: good call. make it adaptive: default max_hold = max(25ms, p95_warmup). runtime telemetry feeds the scheduler.

sam: concerning costs: small-window fastpath reduces latency but increases context switch overhead and more frequent kernel launches. we need a quantifiable cost model exposed in the console so product can measure unit economics.

maria: yes, add telemetry hooks: per-path tokens, kernel-launch-rate, kv-touch-count. those can power Redwood Optimize suggestions.

dina: tradeoff i want recorded: preempting a request mid-window can lose prefix reuse benefits (short term). fallback: if a request had >X kv cache hits, protect it from preempt until complete.

alex: that seems reasonable. maybe a cheap bitflag tracked on admission: protected=true when kv_hits > threshold. simple and cheap.

infra-bot: deploy-note: running an experiment will require a toggle in rollout flags and an observability dashboard. i can create the feature flag and a test dashboard for kernel-launch-rate / tail-latency. :robot_face:

maria: follow-ups i will add to the RFC:
- clear separation of admission vs kv eviction interfaces (with simple function signatures)
- adaptive small-window thresholds fed by p95 warmup telemetry
- soft-lease preemption + requeue semantics and priority aging
- protection bit when kv_hits exceed threshold
- UX: console metrics + Redwood Optimize hook for suggestions

sam: also add a short playbook: how to roll back if we see thrash (metric: kernel_launch_rate spike > 2x baseline + throughput drop).

maria: will do. if nobody objects i'll draft the follow-up RFC today and ping for review. :+1:

alex: go for it. i can review the admission interface section.

dina: i'll review kv_eviction_hint bits.

sam: i'll sanity-check cost-model and telemetry requirements.

maria: thanks all. will post the RFC link when ready.
